title: What Does In-Home Care Cost in Springfield, MO? (Real Prices + Ways to Pay)
short_title: What does in-home care cost in Springfield, MO?
description: Real in-home care prices from Caring Companions in Springfield, Missouri: Wellness Care $30 an hour, Personal Care $32 an hour, Advanced Care $34 an hour. Visits are at least 4 hours, and at least 8 hours a week. Plus the ways families pay: private pay, long-term care insurance, VA benefits, Medicare GUIDE respite, and more.
end: Get an exact number with a free in-home assessment.

parts.head: What does in-home care cost in Springfield, MO?
parts.sub: Real prices, and the ways families pay
parts.text: What does in-home care cost? It's one of the first questions families ask, and it should have a straight answer. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions in Springfield. Here are our real prices, what changes the cost, and the ways families pay.

parts.head: Posted on our website
parts.sub: No sales call needed. Three levels, by the hour.
parts.text: We post our rates right on our website, because you shouldn't need a sales call to find out. There are three levels of care, priced by the hour.

parts.head: Wellness Care: $30 an hour
parts.sub: Company, meals, housekeeping, errands, rides, reminders
parts.text: Wellness Care is thirty dollars an hour. It's for someone who is mostly independent but could use company and a helping hand: meals, light housekeeping and laundry, errands and rides, and medication reminders.

parts.head: Personal Care: $32 an hour
parts.sub: Plus bathing, dressing, toileting and getting around
parts.text: Personal Care is thirty-two dollars an hour. That's everything in Wellness Care, plus hands-on help with bathing, dressing, toileting, and getting around safely.

parts.head: Advanced Care: $34 an hour
parts.sub: Advanced dementia, wandering, Parkinson's, stroke. Still non-medical.
parts.text: Advanced Care is thirty-four dollars an hour, for advanced dementia, wandering, serious mobility challenges, Parkinson's, or stroke. It's still non-medical care, not skilled nursing.

parts.head: Mostly, the hours
parts.sub: At least 4 hours a visit and 8 hours a week
parts.text: What changes the total is mostly the hours. Visits are at least four hours, and at least eight hours a week. So the smallest schedule, two four-hour visits of Wellness Care, comes to two hundred forty dollars a week.

parts.head: Found a lower rate? We'll beat it.
parts.sub: For your first 6 months. New private-pay clients.
parts.text: Found a lower written rate from another professional home care agency, for the same care? Show us, and we'll beat it for your first six months. That's for new private-pay clients.

parts.head: Private pay
parts.text: Most families pay privately, billed at our published rate. But there's often more help out there than people know about.

parts.head: Long-term care insurance
parts.sub: We check the policy and bill the insurance company directly
parts.text: If there's a long-term care insurance policy, it may cover most or all of the cost. We check the benefits, handle the claim paperwork, and bill the insurance company directly.

parts.head: VA benefits
parts.sub: VA Community Care, and Aid and Attendance
parts.text: Veterans may qualify through VA Community Care, where the VA pays us directly. And the Aid and Attendance benefit can add over fourteen hundred dollars a month for a qualifying veteran or surviving spouse.

parts.head: Medicare GUIDE respite
parts.sub: For dementia caregivers: 20 visits a year, 4 hours each
parts.text: Caring for someone with dementia? Medicare's GUIDE program covers respite visits for families who qualify: twenty visits a year, four hours each.

parts.head: Look at CDS
parts.sub: Family can be the paid caregiver. caringcds.com, 417-218-2888
parts.text: If your loved one has Missouri Medicaid, look at Consumer Directed Services, where a family member or friend can be the paid caregiver. Our sister company, Caring Companions CDS, can help. Their number is on the screen.

parts.head: Putting it together
parts.sub: Home equity, life insurance, savings, family sharing
parts.text: Families also use home equity, a life insurance policy, retirement savings, or brothers and sisters splitting the cost. A short talk with a financial advisor or an elder law attorney can help you put it all together.

parts.head: A free in-home assessment
parts.sub: A real quote for your schedule, not an estimate
parts.text: Want an exact number? A free in-home assessment gets you a real quote, based on your schedule and needs, not an estimate.
See all our prices at mo-care.com slash pricing, or call us at (417) 234-8494. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions. Thanks for watching.
